newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China buys 100,000/T spot jet fuel for 4th quarter.
newsitem.headline: China buys 100,000/T spot jet fuel for 4th quarter.

text.p: China has bought a total of 100,000 tonnes of aviation jet fuel from three oil trading companies over the past week for delivery in the fourth quarter, traders said on Wednesday.

They said a European oil trader sold 50,000-55,000 tonnes at a premium of $1.95-$2.00 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) to northeast China, on a two-port discharge basis.
A Dutch trader sold 30,000 tonnes at a $2.10 premium, c-and-f northeast China. A third cargo of 20,000 tonnes was also heard sold into China but the details were unclear.

Some traders said China might have also bought another 100,000 tonnes of jet fuel for September to December delivery three weeks ago. The semi-term cargoes were said to have been awarded through a closed tender issued by China Aviation Oil Supply Corp (CAOSC).

But two parties -- a European major rumoured to have won the tender and China's state-trader assigned to implement the tender -- said the contract was not awarded. The spot purchases were made to replace the tender, they added.
A Chinese source said a Chinese-Australian joint venture company put in the lowest offer into the closed tender, 70-80 cents below other offers.
But the offer was withdrawn when the company could not hedge their postion in the Singapore paper market. They also discovered their offer price was too low in the current high-priced market.
Traders said the Chinese-Australian firm offered $30.20 per barrel, c-and-f northeast China. The next low offer came from the European major at $31.30 per barrel, c-and-f, traders said.
